criteria_quotes: CPT codes covered if selection criteria are met :
Medical Necessity Aetna considers the following interventions medically necessary:
Members with clinical symptoms and a history of conservative management who meet the following criteria:

Documentation of persistent pain and difficulty walking despite at least six months of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional which includes, but may not be limited to:

Bony Correction Bunionectomy Bony correction bunionectomy (e.g., Akin, Chevron, Keller, Lapidus, Mitchell, proximal metatarsal osteotomy procedures, etc.) to treat symptomatic hallux valgus (bunion) in a skeletally mature individual (i.e., after epiphyseal closure) or an individual who is 18 years of age or older when the following criteria is met:

The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following:
A bilateral bunionectomy done at the same time generally is not deemed medically necessary unless extenuating circumstances are present.
Aetna considers bony correction bunionectomy not medically necessary for the following indications:

Surgical Correction of First Metatarsophalangeal (MTP) Joint Surgical correction of the first MTP joint (e.g., hallux rigidus) (including but not limited to arthrodesis (fusion), cheilectomy or the Keller procedure (resection arthroplasty)) when the following criteria are met:

and Documentation of persistent pain and difficulty walking despite at least six months of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional which includes, but may not be limited to:
or Painful hallux rigidus meeting criteria for surgical correction of MTP joint noted above.
or Failed bony correction bunionectomy (e.g., Keller bunionectomy);
answer.submission_route: Fill out Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (in your account at aetna.com, under complaints, grievances and appeals) and fax or mail it. Confirm the address on your denial letter first. Online: aetna.com (Member Complaint and Appeal Form) By fax: 859-425-3379 By phone: 1-800-872-3862, or the number on your card Deadline: Usually 180 days from the denial -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
